content:
maya: quick sync — proposing a 'softburst' admission layer for Dedicated GPU pools. idea: allow short-lived overcommit for latency-sensitive requests with a token decay so tenants can spike without immediate scale-up. thoughts?
liam: +1 to exploring. what's the safety net if spikes persist?
maya: plan is a layered guardrail: 1) short token window (30s) 2) decay schedule (exponential) 3) circuit-breaker to route to shared-hosted fallback if sustained > threshold
sofia: how do we measure "sustained"? per-tenant QPS over 5m? 1m?
maya: leaning 1m average with 5m smoothing for escalation. immediate admission uses 30s tokens. if 1m avg > token_rate * 2 for 3 consecutive windows -> trigger scale intent.
axel: need to be careful with billing and guarantees. Dedicated customers expect isolation — automatic routing to shared-hosted could be surprising. maybe make fallback opt-in per pool?
jun: Agreed. add config flag on pool: allow_softburst_fallback=true/false. default false for enterprise contracts.
liam: can we amortize prewarm credits instead of fallback? like gradually burn prewarm tokens to avoid cross-tenant route.
maya: yes — softburst consumes transient credits from tenant's warmup budget. if budget exhausted, then fallback (if allowed) or enqueue.
sofia: telemetry: we need metrics: softburst_admits, softburst_rejects, softburst_fallbacks, token_balance, avg_latency_post_admit. also SLO signal for tail latency.
axel: rollout concerns: start in noisy-light mode (emit metrics + audit log, no enforcement) -> dry-run for 2 weeks -> opt-in beta -> default off.
jun: operator contract: admission layer reports a deterministic decision log for reconciliation. e.g.:
```
{ tenant: T1, decision: admit|defer|fallback, tokens_used: 12, reason: "burst-credit", ts: 1670000000 }
```
this helps billing + postmortem.
liam: good. also include a fast path in runtime: admitted requests should avoid extra hops (no proxying) to keep p99 low. fallback must be async redirect with a visible header.
maya: note on fairness: token allocation should be tenancy-weighted by SLA tier. small tenants get tiny burst window; PLG gets larger but capped.
sofia: tradeoff: larger softburst reduces cold-starts but raises chance of throttling core steady traffic. we should load-test with synthetic spike patterns.
axel: performance test plan: run 200 tenants with mixed traffic (PLG, SME, Enterprise) and inject 30s spikes at random — measure admission vs scale events and cost delta.
jun: can we express policy via existing DSL? e.g. add:
```
softburst:
  enabled: true
  token_window_s: 30
  decay: exp(0.5)
  fallback_policy: { allow_shared: false }
  escalation: { window_m: 1, multiplier: 2, required_windows: 3 }
```
sofia: looks good. add observability hooks and a per-tenant audit index.
sre-bot: deploy-checklist created: PR#4821 references this thread. dry-run flag = `runtime.softburst.mode=dry_run`.
maya: next steps: I'll draft RFC with DSL + operator API + rollout checklist. action items: liam -> telemetry signals + dashboards; axel -> legal/customer-impact review for fallback; jun -> operator logging schema; sofia -> load test harness.
liam: I'll sketch PromQL for key metrics and a synthetic test generator.
axel: ping me when RFC is up, I'll loop in enterprise success.
maya: thanks all. filing RFC tomorrow, will link here. :thumbsup:
